title: Live drive: a real codex exec seat delivers a node, transcript and landing sha recorded
description:
SPIDR sibling of task-c090faae9fbe438b959e76a08b7dcfdb (architect-b63fabf3, 2026-09-05), carved out on the PATH axis because it is the ONE deliverable in that row whose blocking condition is EXTERNAL and DATED.

WHY IT IS ITS OWN ROW. The parent's DoD-6 explicitly sanctions `report_blocked` when the Codex quota refuses - it is "a real outcome, not a failure of this row". But that outcome would have blocked the toggle UI, the Seats rendering, the Playwright journey and the docs sweep along with it, stranding landed browser work behind a vendor quota. Splitting lets the browser proof land and lets this row wait. Global rail 21 permits a separate row that certifies a capability shipped by rows it does not own; all three are named in dependsOn.

MEASURED AT FILING (2026-09-05): the Codex quota was recorded exhausted until 2026-09-08. `mem:real-codex-limit-available-on-this-host` records the useful inverse - `codex exec` exits 1 with a verbatim usage-limit line, which makes the provider-limit path provable with no seat double. If the quota still refuses when you claim this, that is the expected state, not a surprise.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: one real `codex exec` seat delivering a real node, on UnAI or a fresh project, with the transcript and the landing sha recorded in a row comment (under ~4500 chars; comments truncate SILENTLY at 5000).

WHAT IT DOES NOT OWN: everything that can be proven offline. The scripted-double journey over the real MCP wire is task-ae309e47 and is deliberately quota-free; the browser toggle, Seats rendering and Playwright journey are task-c090faae; the mission parity is task-df64aa20. If any of those is wrong, comment there and report_blocked - do not fix it here.

THE ONE THING THIS ROW ADDS over the offline journey: proof that a REAL codex binary, on a real credential, under the real spawn surface (`--ignore-user-config`, the bearer in the child env, the closed env allowlist, the quote-free `-c` values) completes a node. A scripted double cannot prove that, which is precisely why the offline row exists separately and why this one cannot be replaced by it.

VERIFY: the landing sha, read from the durable ledger after the seat is dead.
definitionOfDone: A REAL `codex exec` seat - not a double, not a shim, not a claude seat - delivered a node end to end. The transcript and the landing sha are recorded in a row comment under ~4500 chars (comments truncate SILENTLY at 5000; put the long tail in a second comment rather than losing it). Name the project and the node.
The landing sha is read from the DURABLE LEDGER after the seat's process is dead, never from the seat's stdout or exit code. Quote the command used to read it and its output.

EVIDENCE THAT IT WAS ACTUALLY CODEX, asserted on the spawn surface rather than on intent: the codex-shaped argv or the bearer-in-env path, quoted from the run. A claude seat reported as a codex one is the single worst outcome available to this row, and the parent's rail names it explicitly.

IF THE QUOTA REFUSES: `moe.report_blocked` with the RESET DATE and the EXACT refusal line, verbatim. That is a COMPLETE and CORRECT outcome for this row, not a failure - do not fabricate a pass, do not substitute a double, and do not let a partial run be reported as a delivery. Re-read `mem:real-codex-limit-available-on-this-host` first: a `codex exec` that exits 1 with the usage-limit line is itself the evidence to quote.

Any defect this run exposes is FILED, NOT FIXED HERE: name the owning row (task-c090faae for the browser, task-df64aa20 for mission parity, task-48932bec for spawn-surface parity) and comment there. This row changes no production file; if it needs to, that is the signal it found work belonging to someone else.
taskRails: A BLOCKED OUTCOME IS A CORRECT OUTCOME. If the Codex quota refuses, report_blocked with the reset date and the exact refusal line. Never fabricate a pass, never substitute a scripted double, and never report a claude seat as a codex one.

THIS ROW CHANGES NO PRODUCTION FILE. It drives what other rows built. A defect it finds is filed against the owning row, not fixed here - if you are editing apps/ to make this pass, stop and file instead.

NEVER WEAKEN THE CODEX SPAWN SURFACE to make the drive succeed: `--ignore-user-config`, the bearer through the env var, the closed env allowlist and the quote-free `-c` values are deliberate. A drive that passes against a relaxed surface certifies a product that does not exist.
NEVER PASTE A CREDENTIAL into the transcript comment. Scrub the environment dump; a credential in a row comment cannot be recalled.
FEATURES ONLY (inherited): no security-boundary or policy work.

implementationPlan.description: THE QUOTA PROBE. DO THIS FIRST AND SPEND NOTHING ELSE UNTIL IT ANSWERS. This row's whole shape turns on one external fact, the probe costs seconds, and setting up the lane first would burn most of a session before learning the answer. Run: `codex exec "say hi"` and capture BOTH streams and the exit code - the refusal prints to STDERR, so a stdout-only capture reads as empty success. MEASURED BY THE ARCHITECT AT PLAN TIME (2026-09-05, this exact command on this host): EXIT=1, and verbatim on stderr `ERROR: You've hit your usage limit. Visit https://chatgpt.com/codex/settings/usage to purchase more credits or try again at Sep 8th, 2026 10:46 AM.` The binary is installed at `/c/Users/Yaron/AppData/Local/Programs/OpenAI/Codex/bin/codex` and `~/.codex/auth.json` exists, so this is a QUOTA refusal, not a missing install and not a missing credential - do not go looking for either. THE PROBE DECIDES THE ROW: (A) EXIT 1 with the usage-limit line -> go to step 2 and STOP THERE; you are done, correctly. (B) EXIT 0 -> the quota reset or credits were bought; go to step 3. (C) Anything else - a missing binary, an auth error, a hang - is NEITHER branch: it is a different failure and it must be reported as itself, with the exact output, never folded into the quota story. Note that this row's dependsOn (task-c090faae, task-df64aa20, task-ae309e47) means you cannot reach WORKING before those land, so by the time you hold this the date may well be past 2026-09-08 and branch (B) may be live - re-measure, never assume either way from this description.

BRANCH A - THE QUOTA STILL REFUSES. THIS IS A COMPLETE AND CORRECT OUTCOME FOR THIS ROW, not a failure, and the row was carved out of task-c090faae precisely so that this outcome strands nothing else. Call `moe.report_blocked` with: the RESET DATE from the refusal line (a date the line states, not one you compute), the EXACT refusal line verbatim including its URL, the exit code, and the command you ran. Do NOT pass blockedOnTaskIds - the wait is on an external quota, not on a board row, and naming an unrelated row would make the runtime auto-unblock this on the wrong signal. Then STOP. Explicitly forbidden, and each of these has a tempting shape: substituting the scripted double from task-ae309e47 (it proves the wire, never the binary - that is why it is a separate row); running a CLAUDE seat and reporting it as codex; reporting a partial run - a seat that spawned and then hit the limit is a limit, not a delivery; and buying credits or changing the account to get past it, which is the operator's decision and not a worker's. ONE THING WORTH DOING IN THIS BRANCH, because it is free and it is real evidence: the refusal is exactly what the provider-limit path consumes, so note in the block reason that this host can still produce a REAL provider limit on demand (`mem:real-codex-limit-available-on-this-host` records the same measurement and its window). That is a fact a later row may need, and the block is the natural place to record that it still holds.

BRANCH B - THE QUOTA ANSWERS. Bring up the live lane. DO NOT USE `scripts/up.ps1` FROM A NON-TTY SHELL: `moe-up-main.ts:357` gives the daemon an operator channel ONLY when `process.stdin.isTTY === true`, so a bash or background launch renders "Moe was started without a terminal it can listen on", `cr.shell.paused` never exists, and you will lose an hour to it. Run the two processes directly instead, exactly as the recipe in `mem:task-task-2723a9b400984ab7b1b10f97c3523c81-handoff` records: `node --experimental-transform-types apps/daemon/src/daemon-main.ts --dependencies=<abs>/apps/daemon/src/daemon-store-dependencies.ts --asset-root=<abs>/apps/control-room/dist --operator-stdin` (daemon-main.ts:220-222 honours `--operator-stdin` on a PIPE; feed the pairing label with `tail -f <file> | node ... daemon-main.ts` and append the label to that file), plus `node --experimental-transform-types apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper-main.ts`. They share only the SQLite store; the wrapper starts its own MCP server and needs no daemon origin. USE A FRESH STORE, NOT THE LIVE ONE: an already-seeded store refuses the second bootstrap at `project.activate` with `BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_BYTES_CONFLICT`. Seed with `node apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/demo-seed-main.ts` and OMIT `MOE_SEED_STOP_BEFORE_APPROVAL` so the drive passes approval and a node actually reaches READY - a seat cannot deliver a node that never became claimable. If you need `/health/read` while debugging, it takes FOUR headers or it refuses before reading: `origin`, `x-moe-csrf`, `x-moe-protocol-version` (from `GENERATED_WIRE_PROTOCOL_VERSION` in the generated client) and `x-moe-session-credential`. Select the provider the way the row under test does: prefer the durable setting from task-8e793ae3 if it has landed, and record which mechanism you used - `MOE_AGENT_COMMAND=codex` still wins at spawn and is the fallback, but say which one drove it, because they are different claims about what works.

BRANCH B - DRIVE ONE NODE AND CAPTURE THE EVIDENCE. Let a REAL codex seat take a node from READY to delivered. WHILE IT RUNS, capture what only the running process can show: the seat's stdout/stderr tail, and the argv or environment evidence that it was CODEX (DoD-3). ASSERT IT ON THE SPAWN SURFACE, NOT ON INTENT - the codex-shaped argv (`exec --ignore-user-config --skip-git-repo-check --ephemeral --sandbox ...`) or the bearer arriving in the child's own environment. Setting `MOE_AGENT_COMMAND=codex` is what you INTENDED; the argv is what HAPPENED, and only the second is evidence. This matters more than it looks: the shim/basename selector means a near-miss silently runs the claude branch (`mem:gotcha-codex-shim-basename-selects-the-provider-and-fails-silently`), and a claude seat reported as codex is the single worst outcome available to this row. THEN, AFTER THE PROCESSES ARE DEAD, read the landing sha from the DURABLE LEDGER (DoD-2) - never from the seat's stdout and never from its exit code. Quote the command you used to read it and its output. Two traps from the same recipe, both already paid for: a stale live child record can wedge an item on pid reuse (`mem:gotcha-a-stale-live-child-record-wedges-an-item-on-pid-reuse`), and a real seat may fail to release its claim (`mem:real-seat-cannot-release-its-claim-2026-09-04`) - if either happens, that is a FINDING to file against the owning row, not something to fix here.

RECORD, OR FILE. (a) THE RECORD (DoD-1): put the transcript and the landing sha in a row comment UNDER ~4500 CHARS - comments truncate SILENTLY at 5000, so a long transcript loses its tail with no warning; split across two comments rather than losing it, and put the sha and the argv evidence in the FIRST one so the load-bearing facts survive. Name the project and the node. SCRUB THE ENVIRONMENT DUMP BEFORE PASTING (row rail 4): the codex seat carries its bearer in the child's own environment, so a raw env dump in a row comment publishes a credential that cannot be recalled - paste variable NAMES and never values, the same distinction `resources-credential.ts` enforces on screen. (b) FILE, DO NOT FIX (row rail 2): this row changes no production file. Anything the drive exposes goes to its owner - task-c090faae for the browser and Seats, task-df64aa20 for mission parity, task-48932bec for spawn-surface parity, task-3a0478f5 for provider resolution at spawn. Comment there with the measurement; if you find yourself editing anything under apps/ to make this pass, STOP - that is the signal you found someone else's work, and the correct output is a comment plus a report, not a diff. (c) THE COMPLETION RECORD must state: which branch the step-1 probe took and its verbatim output; which mechanism selected the provider (durable setting or `MOE_AGENT_COMMAND`) and therefore which claim this run supports; the spawn-surface evidence that it was codex, quoted; the landing sha and the command that read it from the ledger; and every finding filed elsewhere, by row id. (d) IF THE DRIVE FAILS PART-WAY IN BRANCH B - the seat spawns but does not deliver - that is NOT a quota block and must not be reported as one: report what failed with its exact output, file against the owning row, and say plainly that the node did not land. A partial run reported as a delivery is the failure mode this row's rails exist to prevent.

comments.content:
QUOTA RE-MEASURED AT PLAN TIME — STILL DRY. architect-b63fabf3, 2026-09-05. Plan approved: 5 steps, zero files (this row edits nothing).

I ran the probe rather than trusting the 3-day-old memory, because a quota can be topped up at any moment and the whole row turns on it:

```
$ codex exec "say hi"
ERROR: You've hit your usage limit. Visit https://chatgpt.com/codex/settings/usage
to purchase more credits or try again at Sep 8th, 2026 10:46 AM.
EXIT=1
```

**It is a QUOTA refusal, not a setup problem** — the binary resolves at `/c/Users/Yaron/AppData/Local/Programs/OpenAI/Codex/bin/codex` and `~/.codex/auth.json` exists. A worker must not go hunting for a missing install or a missing key.

**The refusal prints to STDERR.** A stdout-only capture reads as an empty success. The plan says so in step 1.

## The plan is a runbook with two fully-written branches, and the ordering is the point

Step 1 is the probe and nothing else. It costs seconds; bringing the lane up first costs most of a session before you learn the answer — that is the expensive mistake available here, and the one a worker keen to make progress would make.

I did **not** plan only the block, even though it is the likelier outcome today: this row's `dependsOn` (task-c090faae, task-df64aa20, task-ae309e47) means it cannot reach WORKING until those land, and by then the date may be past 2026-09-08 with the quota reset. Both branches are written; the worker re-probes and neither this plan nor the memory is trusted over the measurement.

## Three things that are NOT a quota block

A missing binary, an auth failure, and a **partial run** — a seat that spawned and then failed to deliver. Each is its own finding with its own output. The row's worst outcome is a fabricated pass; its second worst is a real defect buried under "quota".

## Two specifics worth flagging

- **No `blockedOnTaskIds` on the block.** The wait is on an external quota, not a board row. Naming one would make the runtime auto-unblock this on the wrong signal and hand a worker a row whose quota is still dry.
- **The bearer rides in the child's environment.** A raw env dump pasted into the transcript comment publishes a credential that cannot be recalled — names, never values. And comments truncate *silently* at 5000 chars, so the sha and the argv evidence go in the first comment.

## One free thing the block branch should record

This refusal is exactly what the provider-limit path consumes. A real provider limit is available on demand on this host until the reset — the block reason is the natural place to note that it still holds, since a later row may need it.

## The evidence standard for "it was codex"

Setting `MOE_AGENT_COMMAND=codex` is what you *intended*; the codex-shaped argv is what *happened*. Only the second is evidence — the basename selector makes a near-miss run the claude branch silently, and a claude seat reported as a codex one is the single worst outcome this row can produce.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
THIS ROW CHANGES NO PRODUCTION FILE, so the plan is a RUNBOOK, not an edit sequence, and its shape is dictated by one external fact.

CHOSEN - PROBE FIRST, BRANCH EXPLICITLY, BOTH BRANCHES FULLY SPECIFIED. The quota probe costs seconds and decides the entire row; the lane setup costs most of a session. Ordering them the other way round is the expensive mistake available here, and it is the one a worker keen to "make progress" would make.
REJECTED - planning only the happy path and leaving the block as an exception: the block is the LIKELIER outcome at filing time (measured, see below) and the row was carved out of task-c090faae precisely so this outcome strands nothing else. A plan that treats it as an exception invites a worker to try to work around it.
REJECTED - planning only the block: the row's dependsOn (task-c090faae, task-df64aa20, task-ae309e47) means it cannot reach WORKING until those land, and by then the date may be past 2026-09-08 and the quota reset. Both branches must be written.
REJECTED - naming blockedOnTaskIds on the block: the wait is on an external quota, not a board row. A named row would make the runtime auto-unblock on the wrong signal - the row would go claimable while the quota was still dry.
REJECTED - allowing the scripted double as a substitute: that is task-ae309e47, deliberately separate and deliberately quota-free. It proves the WIRE; only a real binary proves the binary. Folding them would let the offline row retire a question it cannot answer.

planningNotes.risks:
FIRST - THE EXPENSIVE MISTAKE IS ORDERING. Bringing up the lane before probing the quota burns most of a session to learn a fact available in seconds. Step 1 exists to prevent exactly that.

SECOND - THE REFUSAL IS ON STDERR. A capture that reads stdout only sees nothing and may be misread as success. Capture both streams and the exit code.

THIRD - THREE THINGS THAT ARE NOT A QUOTA BLOCK and must never be reported as one: a missing binary, an auth failure, and a partial run (a seat that spawned and then failed). Each is its own finding with its own output. The row's worst outcome is a fabricated or mislabelled pass, and its second worst is a real defect buried under "quota".

FOURTH - A CLAUDE SEAT REPORTED AS CODEX. The basename selector fails silently, so intent is not evidence. Assert the codex-shaped argv or the bearer-in-env path, from the run.

FIFTH - THE CREDENTIAL RIDES IN THE CHILD'S ENVIRONMENT. A raw env dump pasted into the transcript comment publishes a credential that cannot be recalled. Paste NAMES, never values.

SIXTH - COMMENTS TRUNCATE SILENTLY AT 5000 CHARS. A long transcript loses its tail with no warning; keep each under ~4500 and put the sha and the argv evidence in the FIRST comment so the load-bearing facts survive.

SEVENTH - DO NOT NAME blockedOnTaskIds ON THE BLOCK. The wait is external; a named row would auto-unblock this on the wrong signal and hand a worker a row whose quota is still dry.

EIGHTH - THIS ROW EDITS NOTHING UNDER apps/. If it needs to, it has found someone else's work: file against task-c090faae, task-df64aa20, task-48932bec or task-3a0478f5 and report, rather than fixing.

NINTH - NEVER WEAKEN THE CODEX SPAWN SURFACE to get a pass: `--ignore-user-config`, the env-var bearer, the closed allowlist and the quote-free `-c` values are deliberate. A drive that passes against a relaxed surface certifies a product that does not exist.
